title: From a funded organization into the department that funds it
question: Who was a paid officer or employee of an organization and then joined the City department that pays it?
finding: 8 people new to the payroll since fiscal 2019 share a name with a paid officer or key employee of an organization that their new department went on to pay at least $100,000; 1 is confirmed by their own Form 700.
how: Names are matched only when they behave as one person in the City payroll and are rare (fewer than one other Bay Area resident expected to share the name, from how common each first and last name is among 71,958 City employees; names held by two or more licensed California health providers are dropped). 48,514 of 68,293 payroll names pass. The payroll file names employees only from fiscal 2017. The person must be listed with pay of at least $25,000 on the organization’s tax return in the four years before their first City pay, and the hiring department must have paid the organization in the person’s first three years.
limits: State conflict-of-interest law bars an official from taking part in a decision that affects anyone who paid them $500 or more in the previous twelve months; whether each person stepped aside is not recorded in any dataset. Most rows are name matches.
